heading: Hastings' area law for gapped one-dimensional ground states
lede: In 2007 Hastings proved that the ground state of a gapped one-dimensional quantum chain has bounded entanglement: the entropy of every block of sites is at most a constant independent of the length of the chain, and the ground state is well approximated by a matrix product state. The proof writes the ground-state projector approximately as a product of operators that act on the two sides of a cut and on a window around it, and uses that factorization to show that the mutual information across a cut cannot keep doubling. This page tracks the Lean 4 formalization of that proof, a second proof of a theorem that TNLean already proves by a shorter argument.
description: Progress of the Lean 4 formalization of Hastings' proof of the one-dimensional area law, arXiv:0705.2024.

routes.heading: How Hastings proves the area law
routes.intro: The chain has N sites of local dimension D, nearest-neighbour terms of norm at most J, and a unique ground state Ψ0 with gap ΔE. Set ξ = max(2v/ΔE, ξC), using the Lieb–Robinson velocity v and decay length ξC. The paper sets ξ′ = 6ξ. The restricted construction instead uses ξch = 8 max(2v0/ΔE, 1), where v0 comes from the available chain localization estimate, and reaches ξ′ > 6ξch. Identifying a Lieb–Robinson pair with the source’s support dependence, the endpoint rate and a prefactor polynomial in ξ remain open. The stages below explain the consequences of a factorization error ε(l) = C1e−l/ξ′, keeping these restrictions explicit.

stages.title: Approximate factorization of the ground-state projector
stages.physics: Fix a cut between sites j and j + 1 and a length l. The construction underlying Lemma 1 produces three contractions: OL acting left of the cut, OR acting right of it, and OB acting on the window of 2l sites around it, whose product is within ε(l) = C1 e−l/ξ′ of the projector P0 onto Ψ0 in operator norm. The construction splits H into a left part, a buffer and a right part, centres each at the ground state, and averages each under the time evolution against a Gaussian whose width is set by the gap. The averaged parts nearly annihilate Ψ0; the Lieb–Robinson bound makes them nearly local again. OL and OR are spectral projections of the localized left and right parts onto eigenvalues of small absolute value, and OB is a localized Gaussian average of the evolution in the interaction picture. As the note added to the paper records, this OB need not be positive; Lemma 4 repairs that by passing to OB†OB, at the cost of replacing ε by a constant times √ε.
stages.delivers: The assembled bound is ‖OB OL OR − P0‖ ≤ (a + b√l)e−l/(6ξch), hence ≤ C1e−l/ξ′ for any ξ′ > 6ξch. The left and right factors are orthogonal projections; the window factor is a contraction. The endpoint ξ′ = 6ξ, a Lieb–Robinson estimate with a numerical prefactor and arbitrary second support, and polynomial dependence of C1 on ξ remain unresolved. Making the window factor positive by Lemma 4 changes the error to order √ε(l), with rate e−l/(2ξ′).

stages.title: The bootstrap: entropy from overlap with low Schmidt rank
stages.physics: Suppose a mixture ρ of states of Schmidt rank at most k across the cut has overlap P with the ground state. Applying the factorization at window length m multiplies the Schmidt rank by at most D2m, since OB acts on 2m sites, and leaves a state close to Ψ0. By the variational characterization of the Schmidt coefficients, the weight of Ψ0 beyond its first k D2m Schmidt coefficients is then at most 2C12e−2m/ξ′/P for every m. Maximizing the entropy subject to this whole family of geometric tail constraints bounds the entropy of the half chain.
stages.delivers: Lemma 2: S(ρ01,j) ≤ ln k + ξ′ ln(2C12/P) ln D + F(ξ′, D), with F(ξ′, D) = (ξ′ + 4) ln D + 1 + ln(D2 − 1) + ln(ξ′/2 + 1).

stages.title: Mutual information across a cut
stages.physics: Assume that the high-entropy hypothesis and the bootstrap give p = Tr(P0σ) ≤ 2ε, where σ is the product of the two half-chain marginals. The window effect is E = OB†OB, as in the note added to the paper; OLOR supplies an auxiliary projection, not the measurement on the window. On the ground state, the expectation of E is at least 1 − 4ε. On σ it is at most 20ε when ε ≤ 1/136. Set η = 2ε. A measurement cannot increase relative entropy, and relative entropy with respect to the product of the marginals is mutual information. The resulting binary relative entropy gives the lower bound below; nonnegativity handles larger η.
stages.delivers: Under this overlap hypothesis, the mutual information of the two halves of the window is at least (1 − 2η(l)) l/ξ′ − ln(2C1) − 7, where η(l) = 2C1e−l/ξ′ and 4C1 > 1. This retains the exponential rate without replacing the window factor in the factorization by its positive repair. It is a conditional step in the high-entropy contradiction, not a lower bound for every gapped ground state.

stages.title: The doubling argument
stages.physics: Suppose some half chain had entropy above a large value Smax. Then the entropy stays above 2Smax/3 along a whole window of length l0 of order Smax/ln D. Let Sl be the largest entropy of an interval of length l in that window. Subadditivity alone gives S2l ≤ 2Sl; combining the bootstrap with the mutual-information bound sharpens this to S2l ≤ 2Sl − (1 − 4C1e−l/ξ′) l/ξ′ + ln(2C1) + 7. Each doubling therefore lowers the entropy per site by a fixed amount, while it starts at most at ln D and can never become negative. Only a bounded number of doublings fit, which bounds l0, contradicting the choice of Smax.
stages.delivers: The source-form target, with the corrected doubling constant, is S(ρ01,i) ≤ c0 ξ′ ln ξ′ ln D · 4ξ′ ln D for every i, with a numerical constant c0. The paper prints 2ξ′ ln D; the iteration needs twice as many doublings as printed. Deriving this source-form constant still requires the endpoint rate and polynomial prefactor described above. The constant is exponential in ξ′, hence in J/ΔE; the proof of the other one-dimensional tab gives a constant linear in J/Δ.

routes.heading: Matrix product states and correlations
routes.intro: The same factorization controls more than the entropy. It bounds the small Schmidt coefficients that a matrix product state approximation discards, and it limits how strongly an operator far from a cut can correlate with an operator diagonal in the Schmidt basis of that cut.

stages.title: Decay of the Schmidt coefficients and matrix product states
stages.physics: Order the Schmidt coefficients of Ψ0 across a cut by size. The first k0 = e2S/2 of them carry weight at least one half, where S is the entropy of the half chain, so the bootstrap applies with P = 1/2 and bounds the weight beyond k0D2m by 4C12e−2m/ξ′. Rewritten in terms of the number k′ of coefficients kept, the discarded weight decays like a power of k′/k0. Truncating every cut of the chain to k′ Schmidt vectors then gives a matrix product state of bond dimension k′. The conditional source argument assumes a uniform entropy bound. For the whole chain, choose one integer k0 at least exp(2S)/2 at every cut. The remaining Hamiltonian application must supply both this bound and the factorization with constants uniform in the chain length.
stages.delivers: The Schmidt weight beyond the first k′ coefficients is at most 4C12 e2/ξ′ (k′/k0)−1/(ξ′ ln D), so sequential truncation gives an unnormalized matrix product vector Φ of bond dimension at most k′ with squared Hilbert-space error ‖Φ − Ψ0‖² of order (N − 1) (k′/k0)−1/(ξ′ ln D). The norm error is the square root of this bound. For fixed chain parameters, polynomial bond dimension therefore gives polynomial accuracy. For N < 2 no cut is truncated and Φ = Ψ0; the displayed power-law expression is used for N ≥ 2.

stages.title: Correlations of Schmidt-diagonal operators
stages.physics: An operator BL acting on the left half and diagonal in the Schmidt basis of Ψ0 has a mirror image BR on the right half with BLΨ0 = BRΨ0. Let A act at distance at least l from the cut. Each factor of the approximate factorization nearly fixes Ψ0 and commutes with one of A, BL, BR by its support, so a chain of triangle inequalities moves BL past A at a small cost. Hastings uses this to show that certain expander matrix product states, whose correlations of this kind stay large, are not ground states of gapped chains.
stages.delivers: Lemma 3: |⟨Ψ0, A BL Ψ0⟩ − ⟨Ψ0, A Ψ0⟩⟨Ψ0, BL Ψ0⟩| ≤ 3√(2ε(l)) + ε(l) for contractions A and BL. This is proved from positive approximate factorization. The current Hamiltonian specialization uses a decay length greater than 12ξch; the source rate and polynomial prefactor remain open.

glossary: S(ρ<sub>1,i</sub>) = −Tr ρ log ρ for the reduced density matrix ρ of the ground state on the first i sites, measuring the entanglement across the cut after site i.
The ground state Ψ<sub>0</sub> is unique and every other eigenvalue of H exceeds the ground energy by at least ΔE.
A bound on how far, in a given time, the evolution under a local Hamiltonian can spread an operator acting on a few sites; on a chain it holds with a velocity v and a decay length ξ<sub>C</sub>.

A product O<sub>B</sub>O<sub>L</sub>O<sub>R</sub> approximating the ground-state projector in operator norm. The left and right factors are projections and the window factor is a contraction. Replacing it by O<sub>B</sub><sup>†</sup>O<sub>B</sub> makes all factors positive but incurs a square-root loss in the error.
The number of nonzero terms in the Schmidt decomposition of a vector across a cut, that is, the rank of the reduced density matrix of either side.
An operator on one side of a cut that is diagonal in the Schmidt basis of the ground state across that cut.
I(X : Y) = S(X) + S(Y) − S(X ∪ Y), the relative entropy of the state on X ∪ Y to the product of its marginals.
Relative entropy cannot increase under a quantum channel, in particular under a measurement.

A vector on a chain written as a contraction of one tensor per site, with open ends. Every internal Schmidt rank is at most the corresponding bond dimension. For a nonzero vector on a chain of at least two sites, the minimal possible maximal bond dimension equals the largest Schmidt rank across internal cuts; an arbitrary representation may have larger bonds.
